newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Oct consumer prices rise 1.8 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Canada Oct consumer prices rise 1.8 pct on year.

text.p: Canada's unadjusted October consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the month and 1.8 percent in the year to 136.2, Statistics Canada said Tuesday.
CONSUMER PRICES - Pct chg Oct Sept
Unadjusted ex food and energy mth/mth +0.0 +0.1
Unadjusted ex food and energy yr/yr +1.3 +1.2

A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally adjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month and the undadjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 1.5 percent rise in the all-items and 1.3 percent rise in the core CPI.

Statistics Canada said rising prices for energy, food, new vehicles, post-secondary education and telephone services contributed most to the annual increase in the CPI. The gain was partly offset by declines in mortgage interest charges, new homes and computer equipment.

The monthly increase in consumer prices came from rising costs of energy and food. The cost of energy rose 2.1 percent in October, most of which came from higher charges for natural gas, especially in Ontario, where the average residential bill rose by 22.7 percent on the month. The price of gasoline rose 1.3 percent in October and fuel prices rose 5.7 percent, the largest monthly increase in five years.
Food prices rose an average 0.6 percent in October.
